properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check found this block's committed shape had its notch on the WRONG SIDE -- the committed shape was full-width at the north end and narrowed by dropping its EAST portion further south, but Figure 6.4.2 actually shows the opposite: this block narrows by dropping its WEST portion (which is shorter, ending sooner), while the east portion continues further south. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) and extracted the precise contour (OpenCV) -- a 2-step staircase shape at pixel (1250,734), (1250,801), (1331,801), (1332,876), (1401,876), (1401,734). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed zero overlap with Building 2, Building 12 Plaza, Parcel E1, or the waterfront open space. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (street/curb re-anchoring pass, prompted by a user question about validation process consistency): this block's own north edge was directly confirmed, by rendering it against Esri World Imagery, to sit on top of real, currently-paved, actively-used street pavement (visible lane markings and/or vehicles in the satellite image), not a corner-lot sliver -- one of several Pier 70 blocks found this way after this project switched its real-street reference from OSM (community-traced, name-matched ways) to DataSF's own official Street Centerline / Curbs and Islands datasets (src/street_geometry.py), which for the first time gave an accurate enough curb position to see it. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer (6.8m centerline half-width, empirically measured against real curb data near Pier 70 -- see street_geometry.py); area 1476 -> 786 sq m. The clip's result was a MultiPolygon (the street cut disconnected a 62 sq m sliver from the main body); kept only the larger piece, consistent with how this project has handled the same situation elsewhere (Mission Rock Square, Potrero Block 7). This is a targeted correction of this block's street-facing edge, not a re-verified re-trace of its other edges, which still carry this site's usual diagram-transform uncertainty. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the DataSF identifiers named above (Building 14's footprint under blklot 4052001; Building 12's Assessor parcel blklot 4114010) are our own lookups in DataSF's Building Footprints and Assessor parcels layers, not statements in the D4D, which this file cites only for the diagram. Assessor lot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF acdm-wktn) and its legacy id is carried by 21 building footprints, so the id does not by itself identify Building 14; 4114010 is an active P70-MU lot at 1070 Maryland St that DataSF does not name as Building 12. Nothing in the geometry was changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data -- see digitization_method.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this file uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat. Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026), which says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free fit of the plan figure to the map -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this fit's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential (studio-3BR over 7 levels) + ground-floor retail + townhouses along 21st St, designed by Stanley Saitowitz/Natoma Architects, per the architect's own project page (saitowitz.com/pier-70-parcel-d): 'loft town houses along 21st street. Above are studio, one, two and three bedroom units stacked on seven levels', with a retail space along the grove, Market Square and Maryland Street. A weak secondary source implied a ~2020 completion, which no primary source supports: Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward and that no Phase 1 option parcel has been exercised. The Real Deal (Jul 16, 2026) reports Brookfield's development VP saying additional density would let the company 'break ground in 2027 on its first market-rate apartment building' (350 units, parcel not named), a conditional plan not specific to Parcel D. Treat as NOT yet built.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see the accuracy note for this shape. Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026), which says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward.
